intro.title: Discover
intro.subtitle: Empowering professionals and teams to build practical Scrum capabilities, strengthen collaboration, and deliver meaningful value in today’s evolving workplace.
intro.paragraph1: Institute of Scrum is an independent training provider based in Ontario, Canada, specializing in Agile and Scrum training and certification. Our programs are delivered entirely online and structured to accommodate the learner's own pace.
intro.paragraph2: Our organization is founded on many years of professional experience in Agile and Scrum across North America. This experience shapes every aspect of our programs, from the structure of our learning tracks to the design of our practice and final exams. The outcome is training that is practical, current, and fully aligned with the way Scrum is applied in professional environments today.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.body1: Our mission is to help professionals learn Scrum correctly, reinforce that learning through realistic practice, and earn a certification that reflects genuine competence.
mission.body2: To fulfill this mission, we are committed to:
mission.body3: Delivering clear and practical training materials designed for a global audience. Maintaining fair and transparent pricing, so that cost is never a barrier to professional growth. Designing tests that assess true understanding of Scrum, rather than memorization. Offering every learner a complete package — training, practice, final exam, and digital certificate — within a single, straightforward subscription.

vision.title: Our Vision
vision.body1: We envision a future where practical Scrum knowledge and professional development are within reach for anyone committed to learning, growing, and contributing more effectively in the workplace.
vision.body2: Our vision is to build an inclusive learning community that helps professionals strengthen applied Scrum capabilities, earn meaningful credentials, and use their knowledge with confidence to support better collaboration, adaptability, leadership, and value delivery across teams and organizations.

trackIncluded.title: What You Receive with Your
trackIncluded.subtitle: Each learning track at Institute of Scrum is delivered as a complete package. Your registration includes

items.title: Comprehensive Scrum materials
items.body: Explore the Scrum framework, its roles, events, and artifacts through clear explanations, practical guidance, and relevant examples.

items.title: Access to the final exam
items.body: Your final exam is included at no additional cost and can be completed whenever you feel confident, prepared, and ready.

items.title: A digital certificate
items.body: Issued after successfully passing your final exam.

items.title: All learning is self-paced
items.body: Study at your own pace, revisit the learning materials whenever needed, and complete the final exam when you feel fully confident, prepared, and ready to proceed.

items.title: Mock Exam
items.body: Prepare for the final exam with a focused practice experience designed to strengthen your readiness and help you approach the exam with greater confidence. The mock exam allows you to assess your knowledge, identify topics that may require additional review, reinforce key Scrum concepts, and improve your understanding before proceeding. Its purpose is to help you feel fully prepared and more confident for success.

offer.title: What we
offer.subtitle: At the Institute of Scrum, we offer Scrum and Agile training and certification programs designed to help individuals and organizations build practical, job-ready skills.

cards.title: Scrum Master
cards.body: A Scrum Master supports the Scrum Team by helping them understand and apply Scrum principles effectively. They remove obstacles, facilitate Scrum events, encourage collaboration, and protect the team from distractions. The Scrum Master also coaches the Product Owner, Development Team, and organization to improve Agile practices, team performance, communication, and continuous delivery of value.

cards.title: Product Owner
cards.body: A Product Owner is responsible for maximizing the value of a product by clearly defining priorities, managing the product backlog, and ensuring the development team understands business needs. They act as the bridge between stakeholders and the Scrum Team, making decisions about what should be built next based on customer value, business goals, and feedback.

cards.title: Scrum Facilitator
cards.body: A Scrum Master supports the Scrum Team by helping them understand and apply Scrum principles effectively. They remove obstacles, facilitate Scrum events, encourage collaboration, and protect the team from distractions. The Scrum Master also coaches the Product Owner, Development Team, and organization to improve Agile practices, team performance, communication, and continuous delivery of value.

apart.title: Why Learn
apart.subtitle: Strengthen your knowledge and become familiar with the exam format before taking your final certification exam.

items.title: Practical experience behind your learning
items.body: Our learning is shaped by extensive professional experience in Agile and Scrum. The guidance we provide reflects practical delivery environments, real challenges, and meaningful workplace application.

items.title: Clear language
items.body: Our learning materials use straightforward English, helping professionals understand key Scrum concepts clearly and apply their knowledge with greater confidence.

items.title: A simple learning path
items.body: One enrollment. One learning track. One mock exam. One final exam. One certificate. No hidden fees and no unnecessary complexity.

items.title: Mock Exam Preparation
items.body: A preparation-focused approach. A mock exam is included in every track. It helps you approach the final exam with greater confidence and readiness. Practicing beforehand allows you to identify areas for improvement and strengthen your understanding before proceeding.

items.title: Affordable Fees
items.body: Professional certification can be costly. We have intentionally structured our fees to remain accessible to individual learners, while continuing to provide a quality learning and certification experience.

serve.title: Who We
serve.subtitle: Designed for professionals seeking practical Scrum knowledge, meaningful credentials, and flexible learning that supports career growth.
paragraphs: Our learners come from diverse professional backgrounds, including software developers moving into leadership roles, project managers adopting Agile delivery, business analysts working with Scrum teams, and experienced professionals building capabilities for product, delivery, leadership, and organizational change roles today.

They often share similar priorities: limited time, demanding schedules, and a desire for meaningful certification that strengthens practical skills, builds confidence, and supports future career opportunities.

Whether you are preparing for a Scrum Master role, strengthening your Product Owner capabilities, or expanding your profile with Agile skills, our programs provide practical learning designed to support your goals and growth at every stage.

trust.title: Our Commitment to
trust.subtitle: Confidence begins with clear learning, fair exams, and certification practices designed around consistent professional standards.
paragraphs: Choosing a training provider involves trust. You rely on the quality of the learning materials, the fairness of the exam, and the professional value represented by the certificate as you invest your time and effort in your development.
We take that trust seriously. Our learning content is carefully reviewed before publication, and our exams are maintained to remain aligned with the current Scrum framework.

items.question: Which Scrum certification is right for me?
items.answer: The right certification depends on your current experience, career goals, and the Scrum role you want to develop. The Institute of Scrum offers certification paths for Scrum Masters, Product Owners, and Scrum Facilitators at different competency levels, allowing you to choose the program that best matches your professional development needs.

items.question: Do I need previous Scrum experience to enroll?
items.answer: No. Many Institute of Scrum certification programs are designed to be accessible to learners who are new to Scrum. You can review the details of each certification to choose the level that best matches your current knowledge and professional experience.

items.question: Is there a final exam required to earn the certification?
items.answer: Yes. Certification candidates are required to successfully complete the applicable final exam to demonstrate their understanding of the concepts and competencies covered by the certification program.

items.question: Do Institute of Scrum certifications expire?
items.answer: No. Once you successfully earn an Institute of Scrum certification, the certification does not expire. This means there are no ongoing renewal requirements or recurring certification renewal fees.

intro.title: A Modern Approach to
intro.subtitle: An introduction to the mindset, frameworks, and benefits shaping today's most adaptive organizations
intro.paragraph1: Agile is a mindset and a way of working that helps teams deliver value to customers quickly, iteratively, and in response to change. Rooted in the Agile Manifesto published in 2001, it favors individuals and interactions, working solutions, customer collaboration, and the ability to adapt over rigid plans and heavy processes.
intro.paragraph2: Rather than attempting to define every detail of a project upfront, Agile teams work in short cycles, inspect the results, gather feedback, and adjust their approach. This creates a continuous loop of learning and improvement, allowing organizations to respond to shifting priorities, emerging insights, and evolving customer needs without losing momentum.

frameworks.subtitle: While Agile itself is a philosophy, several frameworks put its principles into practice. The most widely adopted include:

scrum.title: Understanding Scrum
scrum.subtitle: An iterative framework for planning, building, reviewing, and improving work.

refinement.label: Refinement
refinement.body: Keep items clear, sized, and ready.

top.label: Sprint Planning
top.body: Choose the goal and plan the sprint.

top.label: Sprint Backlog
top.body: Selected items broken into actionable work.

bottom.label: Continuous Improvement
bottom.body: Learning from each sprint informs the next cycle.

bottom.label: Sprint Retrospective
bottom.body: Reflect and improve the way of working.

bottom.label: Increment
bottom.body: A usable outcome that meets the definition of done.

bottom.label: Scrum Team
bottom.body: Cross-functional team delivers value during the sprint.

kanban.title: Kanban
kanban.subtitle: Flow-based approach for continuous delivery.
kanban.footer: Suits teams with a steady stream of incoming requests.

practices.title: Test-driven development
practices.body: Write tests first. Build better code.

practices.title: Delivering Maximum Value
practices.body: Provide the right value with minimum effort.

why.title: Why Agile Is
why.paragraph1: Today's business environment is defined by rapid change, digital disruption, and rising customer expectations. Traditional project management approaches, which rely on long planning cycles and fixed scopes, often struggle to keep pace. Agile addresses this challenge by empowering teams to learn quickly, pivot when needed, and deliver working solutions early and often.
why.paragraph2: More than a set of practices, Agile fosters a culture of transparency, collaboration, and accountability. It invites teams to experiment, measure outcomes, and continuously improve, which drives both innovation and employee engagement.
why.imageAlt: Illustration of a person standing confidently

whenWhere.title: When and Where to Use
whenWhere.paragraph1: Agile is particularly effective in environments where requirements are likely to evolve, where customer feedback is critical, and where speed of delivery matters. While it originated in software development, Agile has expanded far beyond IT and is now widely used in marketing, product development, human resources, finance, education, and even manufacturing.
whenWhere.paragraph2: Agile is most valuable when the problem is complex, when the solution is not fully known at the outset, and when innovation is a priority. In contrast, highly predictable, repetitive, or heavily regulated work may benefit from a blended approach that combines Agile with traditional methods.
whenWhere.imageAlt: Illustration of a person raising a sign

benefits.title: Key Benefits of
benefits.intro: Organizations that embrace Agile consistently report meaningful improvements across delivery, culture, and customer outcomes. The most notable benefits include:

items.title: Faster time
items.body: Through incremental delivery and shorter feedback cycles.

items.title: Greater Adaptability
items.body: In responding to changing priorities, market shifts, and customer needs.

items.title: Higher-Quality Outcomes
items.body: Driven by continuous testing, review, and improvement.

items.title: Improving Customer Satisfaction
items.body: Through close collaboration and early, frequent value delivery.

items.title: Stronger Team Engagement
items.body: As people are empowered to own their work and contribute ideas.

items.title: Reduce Risk
items.body: By surfacing issues early and delivering in small, manageable increments.

coreValues.subtitle: The principles that guide adaptive, customer-focused teamwork.
items: Responding to change over following a fixed plan
Individuals and interactions over processes and tools

finalThoughts.title: Final
finalThoughts.body: Agile is not a silver bullet, nor is it simply a set of ceremonies or tools. It is a way of thinking about work, people, and value. Successful Agile adoption requires leadership commitment, cultural change, and a willingness to learn and improve continuously. When embraced authentically, Agile helps organizations build better products, develop stronger teams, and stay relevant in a world that never stops changing.

intro.description: An introduction to the roles, events, and artifacts that help teams turn complexity into outcomes
intro.imageAlt: Team collaborating in front of a sticky-note board during a Scrum session

whatIs.para1: Scrum is a lightweight framework that helps people, teams, and organizations generate value through adaptive solutions to complex problems. First formalized by Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland in the early 1990s, Scrum has become the most widely adopted Agile framework in the world, used by millions of practitioners across industries.
whatIs.para2: At its core, Scrum is built on empiricism and lean thinking. Decisions are based on observation, experimentation, and evidence rather than detailed upfront predictions. Scrum teams work in short, focused cycles, inspecting their progress frequently and adapting as they learn. The framework is deliberately simple, yet it requires discipline and commitment to apply well.

framework.subtitle: Iterative delivery. Collaborate daily. Inspect and adapt continuously.
framework.step2Desc: Ordered list of work to deliver value.
framework.step3Desc: Plan the work for the upcoming sprint.
framework.step4Desc: Selected work broken down into tasks.
framework.step5Desc: Collaborate, build and deliver value every sprint.
framework.step7Desc: Inspect the increment and gather feedback from stakeholders.
framework.step8Desc: Reflect on the sprint and identify ways to improve.
framework.dailyScrumDesc: 15-minute sync to align and remove blockers.
framework.loopDesc: Insights and learnings drive improvements in process, teamwork, and product.

accountabilities.subtitle: Three key roles that help Scrum teams deliver value.
accountabilities.productOwnerDesc: Maximizes the value of the product by managing the Product Backlog, setting priorities, and ensuring the team is working on the most important items.
accountabilities.scrumMasterDesc: Serves as a true leader who coaches the team, removes impediments, and helps the organization embrace Scrum thinking and practice.
accountabilities.developersDesc: A cross-functional group of professionals who build the product increment, own the quality of their work, and collaborate to meet the Sprint Goal.
accountabilities.banner: Together, these accountabilities work collaboratively to deliver valuable product increments.

events.subtitle: Three key roles that help Scrum teams deliver value.
events.sprintPlanningDesc: The team defines the Sprint Goal and decides what work will be delivered.
events.dailyScrumDesc: A short, focused meeting where Developers inspect progress and adapt the plan.
events.sprintReviewDesc: The team and stakeholders inspect the increment and discuss what to do next.
events.sprintRetrospectiveDesc: The team reflects on how to improve its ways of working.
events.sprintDesc: The heartbeat of Scrum, where ideas are turned into value.
events.closingPart1: Together, these events help Scrum teams

artifacts.subtitle: Three key roles that help Scrum teams deliver value.
artifacts.productBacklogDesc: An ordered list of everything that might be needed in the product, committed to a Product Goal.
artifacts.sprintBacklogDesc: The set of items selected for the Sprint, plus the plan for delivering them, committed to the Sprint Goal.
artifacts.incrementDesc: A concrete step toward the Product Goal, usable and meeting the team's Definition of Done.

why.description: Organizations turn to Scrum because it brings structure to complexity without sacrificing agility. By delivering small, valuable increments on a predictable cadence, teams reduce risk, surface problems early, and build confidence with stakeholders. Scrum also fosters transparency, alignment, and a strong sense of shared ownership, helping organizations move faster while staying focused on what matters most to customers.
why.imageAlt: Professional pointing at a Kanban board while preparing for a certification exam

when.description: Scrum is designed for complex work where more is unknown than known and where requirements are likely to evolve. It is especially effective for product development, software delivery, and innovation initiatives, but it is also applied successfully in marketing, research, education, and operations. Scrum works best when a dedicated, cross-functional team can focus on a clear product or outcome, with regular access to stakeholders and end users. For simple, highly repetitive, or purely transactional work, other approaches may be more efficient.
when.imageAlt: Two colleagues reviewing sticky notes on a whiteboard together

benefits.description: How Scrum improves delivery, transparency, quality, alignment, engagement, and risk management.
benefits.fasterDesc: Through short, focused Sprints that produce usable increments.
benefits.transparencyDesc: Across work, progress, and priorities for the team and stakeholders.
benefits.qualityDesc: Through continuous inspection, clear Definitions of Done, and frequent feedback.
benefits.alignmentDesc: between business goals, customer needs, and team execution.
benefits.engagedDesc: Teams self-manage, own outcomes, and continuously improve.
benefits.riskDesc: By validating ideas early and adjusting direction based on real evidence.

intro.description: Project management is the practice of planning, organizing, and guiding work from start to finish — ensuring the right things get done, on time, and within budget. In a world where businesses juggle competing priorities at every turn, it has become one of the most essential disciplines driving efficiency, innovation, and results across every industry.
intro.badgesAlt: ESM, ESM-P, and ESM-A certification badges

whyMatters.title: Why Scrum Master Matters
whyMatters.point1: Organizations lose an average of 11.4% of their investment due to poor project management — Scrum Masters directly reduce that risk.
whyMatters.point2: Scrum Masters act as a shield for their teams, enabling developers to focus on delivering value without distraction.
whyMatters.point3: They foster a culture of transparency, inspection, and adaptation — the core pillars that make Agile transformation sustainable.

faq.q1: Which Scrum certification is right for me?
faq.a1: The right certification depends on your current experience, career goals, and the Scrum role you want to develop. The Institute of Scrum offers certification paths for Scrum Masters, Product Owners, and Scrum Facilitators at different competency levels, allowing you to choose the program that best matches your professional development needs.
faq.q2: Do I need previous Scrum experience to enroll?
faq.a2: No. Many Institute of Scrum certification programs are designed to be accessible to learners who are new to Scrum. You can review the details of each certification to choose the level that best matches your current knowledge and professional experience.
faq.q3: Is there a final exam required to earn the certification?
faq.a3: Yes. Certification candidates are required to successfully complete the applicable final exam to demonstrate their understanding of the concepts and competencies covered by the certification program.
faq.q4: Do Institute of Scrum certifications expire?
faq.a4: No. Once you successfully earn an Institute of Scrum certification, the certification does not expire. This means there are no ongoing renewal requirements or recurring certification renewal fees.

eligibility.heading: Eligibility
eligibility.body: You must be at least 18 years old (or the age of majority in your jurisdiction) to create an account and enroll in certification programs. By registering, you confirm that the information you provide is accurate and complete.

accountRegistration.heading: Account Registration
accountRegistration.intro: To access certain features, you must create an account. You agree to:
items: Maintain the confidentiality of your login credentials
Accept responsibility for all activities under your account
accountRegistration.outro: We reserve the right to suspend or terminate accounts that violate these Terms.

useOfServices.heading: Use of Services
useOfServices.intro: You agree to use the Services only for lawful purposes. You may not:
items: Copy, reproduce, or distribute course materials without authorization
Share exam content, questions, or certification materials
Attempt to disrupt platform security or functionality
useOfServices.outro: All learning materials, exams, and certifications are protected by intellectual property laws.

certification.heading: Certification and Examinations
certification.intro: Certification is granted upon successful completion of required training and passing the official examination.
items: Cancel or invalidate exam results in cases of misconduct
certification.outro: Certification does not guarantee employment or professional advancement.

payments.heading: Payments and Refunds
payments.intro: All fees are clearly displayed prior to purchase. By enrolling, you agree to pay the listed fees.
payments.body: Refund policies, where applicable, are governed by the specific terms provided at the time of purchase. Examination fees may be non-refundable once the exam has been accessed or scheduled.

intellectualProperty.heading: Intellectual Property
intellectualProperty.body: All content on the platform—including text, graphics, videos, exam materials, logos, and certificates—is the property of the organization or its licensors. Unauthorized use, duplication, or distribution is strictly prohibited.

liability.heading: Limitation of Liability
liability.intro: The Services are provided “as is” without warranties of any kind. We do not guarantee uninterrupted access or error-free functionality.
liability.reserveIntro: To the maximum extent permitted by law, we are not liable for:

indemnification.heading: Indemnification
indemnification.body: You agree to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless us, our affiliates, and our respective officers, directors, employees, and agents from any claims, damages, liabilities, costs, or expenses arising out of your use of the Services.

termination.heading: Termination
termination.body: We reserve the right to suspend or terminate your access to the Services at any time, without notice, if we believe you have violated these Terms or applicable law.

governingLaw.heading: Governing Law
governingLaw.body: These Terms shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the jurisdiction in which we operate, without regard to its conflict of law principles.

infoWeCollect.heading: Information We Collect
infoWeCollect.body: We collect information necessary to provide and improve our Services.

personalInfo.heading: Personal Information
items: Payment information (processed securely via third-party providers)

howWeUse.heading: How We Use Your Information
items: Provide access to courses and certification exams
Track learning progress and performance analytics
Communicate important updates and support responses
Improve platform functionality and user experience
Ensure exam integrity and prevent misconduct
howWeUse.outro: We do not sell your personal data.

dataRetention.heading: Data Retention Policy
dataRetention.body: We retain your information for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes outlined in this policy. When your data is no longer needed, we will securely delete or anonymize it.

thirdParty.heading: Third-Party Sharing
thirdParty.body: We may share your information with third parties to assist in providing our services, including payment processors and customer support. We ensure these parties comply with strict data protection standards.

security.heading: Security Measures
security.body: We implement robust security measures to protect your personal data from unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction, including encryption and access controls.

yourRights.heading: Your Rights
yourRights.body: You have the right to access, correct, or delete your personal data. You can also request restrictions on processing and withdraw consent at any time.

cookies.heading: Cookies and Tracking Technologies
cookies.body: We use cookies and similar technologies to enhance user experience, analyze site usage, and deliver targeted advertisements. You can manage cookie preferences through your browser settings.

international.heading: International Data Transfers
international.body: Your information may be transferred to and processed in countries outside your own. We ensure that such transfers are compliant with applicable data protection laws.

changes.heading: Changes to This Policy
changes.body: We may update this privacy policy from time to time. We will notify you of any significant changes and encourage you to review the policy periodically.

contactUs.heading: Contact Us
contactUs.body: If you have any questions or concerns regarding this policy or our data practices, please contact our support team directly through the platform.
